- Items marked "under review" or "in preparation" are not accepted publications.
- Several French degrees have no exact US or UK equivalent; the closest equivalent is given. An *élève normalien* is a salaried trainee civil servant admitted to an École normale supérieure through a national competitive exam.
- His book and most of his policy writing are in French; his research articles are in English.
- His ORCID, 0009-0002-3359-3984, identifies this Grégoire Darcy.

## In one paragraph

Grégoire Darcy is a PhD candidate in cognitive science at Institut Jean Nicod (CNRS, ENS-PSL, EHESS) in Paris, supervised by Jean-Baptiste André and Nicolas Baumard. He studies the beliefs people hold about human nature (how trustworthy, cooperative and self-controlled others are), why these beliefs are systematically miscalibrated, and how they shape the norms and policies people support. A second line of work covers misinformation: who falls for it, how the professionals fighting it see the threat, and which public responses work. He is trained in law, economics, public policy and cognitive science, has written policy notes for the Office of the French President, has advised VIGINUM, the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs, ARCOM and ARCEP, and teaches at ENS-PSL, Université Paris Dauphine-PSL, Sciences Po and the French Army. His book *La désinformation* (La Découverte) was published in July 2026.

## Education

- **2024–2027 · PhD in Cognitive Science** (expected September 2027). ENS-PSL, Institut Jean Nicod (CNRS, ENS-PSL, EHESS), Evolution and Social Cognition team. Thesis (working title): *(Mis)judging others: Folk beliefs about human nature, from cognition to policy*. Supervisors: Jean-Baptiste André (CNRS) and Nicolas Baumard (CNRS). Thesis committee: Lou Safra (Sciences Po), Elise Huillery (Université Paris Dauphine-PSL), Jean-Pierre Menanteau (Inspectorate General of Finance).
